apps.name: SkyRadar
apps.subtitle: ATC-style aircraft radar
apps.localizedDescription:
A real-time air traffic radar scope for your local airspace.

Connects to a local docker-adsb-ultrafeeder receiver over HTTP or HTTPS, with automatic fallback to public ADSB feeds when the receiver is unreachable. The scope orients to the compass so traffic appears where you are actually looking. Tap any aircraft for callsign, altitude, speed, heading, type, and operator.

versions.localizedDescription:
• Fixed the horizon line tilting as you panned left and right
• Fixed the sky view camera staying portrait when the phone was turned, which left the image and the aircraft markers disagreeing
• The camera image now follows the phone as you rotate it
• Aircraft should now sit in the correct part of the sky as you look around

• New sky view: tap SKY on the radar to see aircraft overlaid on the real sky through the camera
• Turn the phone sideways — landscape is now supported
• Tap any aircraft in the sky for its full details
• Separate visibility and minimum-altitude controls, so you can match what you can actually see
• Compass correction: tap Calibrate, then tap an aircraft you can genuinely see, and the whole sky lines up
• A warning appears when the compass needs a figure-of-eight calibration
• Aircraft are drawn accounting for the Earth's curvature, which matters for distant low traffic

• Pinch the radar to zoom in and out — handy for picking apart a cluster overhead
• Zoom settles on round range steps and is remembered, so it survives leaving the app
• New orientation chip on the radar: tap to lock the scope north-up, tap again for heading-up
• "Lock North Up" is also available in Settings under Radar Display

• Aircraft are now projected forward from their last report, so blips sit where the aircraft is rather than where it was
• Blips move continuously instead of jumping once per refresh
• Turning aircraft are tracked through the turn, not just straight ahead
• Markers fade as a report ages, and stop moving once too old to predict honestly
• New "Predict Positions" switch in Settings under Data Refresh

• Private trackers are now a list — add several receivers and switch between them
• Each receiver has its own name, shown on the radar status badge instead of "LOCAL"
• Indicator light per receiver shows reachability at a glance, with a Test All button
• Receiver URLs drop the port when it is the scheme default
• Switching a receiver to HTTPS moves port 80 to 443 automatically
• Existing receiver settings migrate across automatically
